bare_s1.explanation: The unit responds broadly to man-made, often handcrafted or decorated objects such as fabric items, ornaments, accessories and gear. It may be keyed to curved, bordered or seamed contours, or to ornamental patterns on those objects, but no single concept is clear.

bare_s2.explanation: The unit appears to respond to the surfaces of close-up, product-style photos of man-made objects, most strongly crafted or decorated items such as textiles, ornaments, embossed or patterned surfaces, and accessories. Plainer manufactured objects like the mouse, knee pads and shoes look like weaker extensions of the same theme.

Q0_s1.explanation: The unit seems to mix at least two unconnected features: ornamental, often floral or stitched decorative patterns on crafted objects (crochet, brooch, manhole cover, teapot carving, bib, basket, Christmas stocking) and smooth, glossy dark molded surfaces (computer mouse, knee pads, toy gun, armor). Its common ground is only broad: close-up photos of man-made objects.

Q0_s2.explanation: The unit seems to respond to close-up views of handcrafted or decorated man-made objects, especially fabric and sewn items such as stockings, cushions, bibs, bow ties and crochet. It extends more weakly to other ornamented or smooth-edged objects like armor, a teapot, a manhole cover and a computer mouse.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds to smooth, rounded, arc-shaped contours where a curved surface meets its border, especially when that border is outlined, trimmed or stitched. It responds more weakly to ornamental radial motifs made of repeated lobed shapes spreading from a center.

F1_s2.explanation: The unit responds mainly to smooth, uniformly colored crafted surfaces bounded by crisp curved outlines or seams. It responds more weakly to flat, stylized decorative motifs such as radial petal-like shapes, stars and printed patterns on those surfaces.

wrong.explanation: The unit mainly responds to thin, upright vertical structures such as screw shafts, tail fins, masts, antennas, handles and slots, mostly on man-made objects. It responds more weakly to vertical frame edges like car and tractor cab window pillars.
